icd10_codes.description: Concussion with loss of consciousness of 30 minutes or less, initial encounter
Laceration without foreign body of scalp, initial encounter
Fall (on) (from) unspecified stairs and steps, initial encounter
Restaurant or cafe as the place of occurrence of the external cause

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , mr . {PATIENT_LAST} . how are you ?
[patient] hello . well , i've got a pretty good headache , i'll tell you that .
[doctor] i bet . and is this your wife ?
[patient] yes , this is {OTHER_FIRST} .
[doctor] nice to meet you . so , i'm going to tell dax a little bit about you . mr . {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation on apixaban who presents after a fall down some stairs with a head injury . so tell me what happened last night .
[patient] so we were out to dinner at the {ORG} restaurant downtown , celebrating our fiftieth anniversary . and the restrooms are down a flight of stairs . i was going down and i missed a step , and i fell down the stairs . i think i went down about six or seven steps .
[doctor] okay . and did you hit your head ?
[patient] i hit the back of my head on the bottom step . the waiter said there was a lot of blood .
[doctor] and did you lose consciousness ?
[patient] i think so . i do n't remember hitting the floor . {OTHER_FIRST} says i was out for maybe a minute .
[patient] it was about a minute , maybe less . he was n't making sense at first , he kept asking what restaurant we were at .
[doctor] okay . so a brief loss of consciousness and some confusion afterwards . had you been drinking at all ?
[patient] one glass of wine with dinner . that's it .
[doctor] okay . and did you feel dizzy or lightheaded before you fell , or any chest pain or palpitations ?
[patient] no , no . i just missed the step . the lighting was bad on those stairs .
[doctor] alright . so how have you been feeling since then ?
[patient] i've had a headache all morning , kind of a dull ache in the back of my head . i felt sick to my stomach last night but i did n't throw up . and i feel a little foggy , like i'm a step behind .
[doctor] any trouble with your vision , any weakness or numbness in your arms or legs ?
[patient] no , my vision's fine . no weakness .
[doctor] okay . and what about the cut on your head , what did you do for that ?
[patient] they gave us a towel at the restaurant and we held pressure on it . it stopped bleeding after a while , but it opened up again this morning when i took a shower .
[doctor] okay . and you're still taking your apixaban , five milligrams twice a day ?
[patient] yes , i took it last night and this morning .
[doctor] and how's the afib been otherwise ? any palpitations , shortness of breath ?
[patient] no , i do n't really feel it . my cardiologist says my rate has been good on the metoprolol .
[doctor] good , you're on metoprolol twenty five milligrams twice a day . and you mentioned last time you're retired now ?
[patient] yes , i was an airline pilot for thirty two years . now i mostly do crossword puzzles .
[doctor] well , we'll make sure your brain is in good shape for those . okay , let's go ahead and examine you .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] hey dax , show me the vital signs . so your blood pressure is one thirty six over seventy eight , and your heart rate is seventy six and irregular , which is expected with your atrial fibrillation . okay , i'm going to look at the back of your head . so there's a laceration on the occipital scalp , it's about four centimeters long . it's gaping a little bit and there's some oozing , but no active arterial bleeding . there's no debris in it . i'm going to press around the edges . i do n't feel any step-off of the skull .
[patient] it's sore .
[doctor] i know . now follow my finger with your eyes . good . your pupils are equal and reactive . can you squeeze my hands ? push down with your feet ? good , strength is normal and equal . touch your nose and then my finger . good . no drift . you're oriented , you know the date and where you are , but you were a little slow with the serial sevens . does your neck hurt when i press on it ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay , no cervical spine tenderness .
[doctor] so because you're on a blood thinner and you lost consciousness , we did a ct scan of your head and your neck this morning . hey dax , show me the ct head . the ct of your head shows no bleeding in the brain and no skull fracture . there's some swelling of the scalp where you hit it . the ct of the neck is normal .
[patient] oh , thank goodness .
[doctor] yes , that's very reassuring . so for my assessment and plan . first , you have a concussion with a brief loss of consciousness of under thirty minutes . i want you to rest your brain for the next couple of days , limit screen time and reading , no driving for at least a week , and no alcohol . you can use tylenol for the headache , but avoid ibuprofen or aspirin , because you're already on a blood thinner . if you get worse headache , repeated vomiting , confusion , or weakness , you need to come back to the emergency room right away .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] second , the scalp laceration . we'll irrigate it and close it with staples today . the staples come out in about seven to ten days . keep it dry for a day , and then you can shower .
[patient] alright .
[doctor] third , your atrial fibrillation . since the ct is negative , i'd continue the apixaban and the metoprolol . and {OTHER_FIRST} , i'd like someone to stay with him for the next twenty four hours .
[patient] i'm not going anywhere .
[doctor] perfect . hey dax , finalize the note .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Head injury after a fall down stairs.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation on apixaban who presents after a fall down stairs on {DATE_NUM}. He was at a restaurant and missed a step while walking down a flight of stairs to the restroom, falling down approximately 6 to 7 steps and striking his occiput on the bottom step. His wife, {OTHER_FIRST}, reports loss of consciousness for approximately 1 minute followed by transient confusion. He had 1 glass of wine. He denies preceding dizziness, lightheadedness, chest pain, or palpitations.

Since the event, he reports a dull occipital headache, nausea without vomiting, and feeling foggy. He denies visual changes, focal weakness, or numbness. The scalp wound was controlled with pressure but reopened this morning. He has taken his apixaban as scheduled.

His atrial fibrillation is followed by cardiology and is rate controlled on metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Retired airline pilot. Drinks alcohol socially.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vitals: BP 136/78, HR 76 irregular.
Head: 4 cm laceration of the occipital scalp with mild oozing, no active arterial bleeding, no foreign body. No palpable skull step-off.
Neck: No cervical spine tenderness.
Neuro: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements intact. Strength 5/5 and symmetric. Finger-to-nose intact. No pronator drift. Oriented. Slowed serial sevens.
Cardiovascular: Irregularly irregular rhythm.

RESULTS

CT head without contrast: No intracranial hemorrhage. No skull fracture. Occipital scalp soft tissue swelling.

CT cervical spine: Normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Concussion with loss of consciousness of less than 30 minutes.
- Cognitive rest, limit screen time, no driving for at least 1 week, no alcohol.
- Tylenol as needed for headache. Avoid NSAIDs and aspirin.
- Return precautions reviewed. Wife to stay with the patient for 24 hours.

2. Laceration of the scalp without foreign body.
- Irrigation and staple closure performed today.
- Staple removal in 7 to 10 days.

3. Atrial fibrillation.
- Continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily and metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily.
